I have not launched and will not launch any cryptocurrency token. Any token using this project’s name is not affiliated with me, and I do not endorse it or accept fees from it. Star this repo!* Left: a TikTok ad shot on a phone. Right: an AI remake with another product. rea-video's verdict: the left is all live footage, one set and two camera positions; the right is all AI, 8 shots across 3 generations.
## Quick start rea-video is built for AI agents. In Claude Code, Codex or any agent that can run commands, say: ```text Install https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video, then break down this video: /path/to/video.mp4 ``` The agent installs the CLI, learns the workflow and runs the whole thing. You need ffmpeg and Python 3.10+. You can also install rea-video as an agent plugin, which adds its skill to your agent: ```bash # Codex codex plugin marketplace add JuneYaooo/rea-video codex plugin add rea-video@rea-video # Claude Code claude plugin marketplace add JuneYaooo/rea-video claude plugin install rea-video@rea-video ``` `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is the agent-agnostic marketplace entry. The agent still installs the CLI the first time it runs a breakdown. Breakdowns are fully upgraded. Each one gives you two outputs: - **Report** (`report.html` / PDF), for you: more reader-friendly, with a clearer structure, easier to learn from and to understand how the video was made and how to remake it. - **[VIDEO.md](https://videomd.github.io/videomd/)**, for your AI: layered, so the AI reads only what a question needs and uses fewer tokens. picks.name: agent_skills
picks.readme:
# Agent skills from Jane Street

A collection of skills for AI agents and chatbots.
Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file
with instructions for the agent.

## Skills

- **socratic-tutor** — turns an LLM into a strict personal tutor that teaches a
  topic of your choice using the Socratic method: a diagnostic, a skill map with
  levels 0-5, one question at a time, spaced review, and a final assessment.

## How to use

With a coding agent that supports the common `SKILL.md` format, copy the skill
directory into your agent's skills folder, then ask the agent to use it
("teach me X").

With a plain chatbot, paste the body of the skill's `SKILL.md` into the chat
(or into a custom/system prompt), followed by what you want it to do.

## Contributing

These skills are exported from our internal repository, where we use them day to
day, and we hope it's interesting to share that experience more widely. Since
we're trying to share what _we've_ found to be useful, we're not looking for new
skills or for pull requests that change the text of existing ones. If you've
adapted a skill and it works better for you, that's great, but please keep your
own copy.

Issues are welcome if something doesn't work as described, though we may not be
able to act on all of them.

## Prior art

Teaching by asking questions is the
[Socratic method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socratic_method), which is
rather older than LLMs, and there are other tutoring prompts and skills built on
the same idea. Our skill was written internally and isn't knowingly derived from
any other implementation.

picks.name: ub-mode
picks.readme:
# ub-mode

`ub-mode` is an agent skill that enforces disciplined software engineering principles when writing or changing code. It is loosely based on portions of [@poteto](https://github.com/poteto)'s rules (`poteto-mode` / `pstack`), reduced and paired with deterministic quality-gate tools:

1. **First Make it Work** — Laziness Protocol, Foundational Thinking, TDD, Redesign From First Principles, Attack the Premise, Subtract Before You Add, Outcome-Oriented Execution, Build the Lever, and Architecture (Model the Domain, Boundary Discipline, Type System Discipline, Make Operations Idempotent, Separate Before Serializing Shared State).
2. **Then Make it Right** — Fix Root Causes, Sequence Work into Verifiable Units, Test Behavior (Not Implementation), [Crapper](https://github.com/unclebob/crapper) (`CRAP < 10`), [Dryer](https://github.com/unclebob/dryer) (duplication `< 0.8`), [Mutator](https://github.com/unclebob/mutator) (cover the uncovered, kill the survivors, delete dead code), and Refactoring.
3. **Practice** — Keep a Log, Guard the Context Window, Worktree Cleanup, and Commit and Push in small ordered commits.

## Companion Tool Repositories

`ub-mode` relies on deterministic quality-gate tools to enforce structure, complexity, duplication, and test thoroughness:

- [unclebob/crapper](https://github.com/unclebob/crapper) — Computes cyclomatic complexity, test coverage, and CRAP score per function so every function stays under the CRAP threshold (`< 10`).
- [unclebob/dryer](https://github.com/unclebob/dryer) — Detects structural code duplication so duplicate blocks (`>= 0.8` similarity) are eliminated.
- [unclebob/mutator](https://github.com/unclebob/mutator) — Runs mutation testing to expose uncovered code and surviving mutants that tests fail to catch.
- [unclebob/uml-viewer](https://github.com/unclebob/uml-viewer) — Visualizes components, coverage, CRAP, mutation scores, and dependency directions.

## Installation

Copy `SKILL.md` into your agent's skills directory as `ub-mode/SKILL.md` (for example `~/.grok/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`, `~/.claude/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`, or `~/.cursor/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`), then invoke `/ub-mode`.

picks.desc: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
picks.readme:
### The open protocol that connects any agent to any app. **[Docs](https://docs.ag-ui.com)** · **[Examples](https://dojo.ag-ui.com)** · **[Spec](https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0)** · **[Discord](https://discord.gg/Jd3FzfdJa8)**

**AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.** Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack. > [!IMPORTANT] > **AG-UI 1.0 is here.** The protocol now has a stable, frozen [specification](https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0) backed by a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs are generated from it. 1.0 is backwards compatible in both directions: 0.x agents work with 1.0 clients and vice versa. [What changed →](https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0/changelog) · [Migration guide →](https://docs.ag-ui.com/migrating-to-1-0) ## Quick start **Start a new app.** The CLI scaffolds a frontend ([CopilotKit](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit) on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick: ```bash npx create-ag-ui-app@latest ``` Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before `npm run dev`: ```bash export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..." ```
Or speak the protocol directly: a 30-line agent server and client
An AG-UI agent is any HTTP endpoint that accepts a `RunAgentInput` and streams events back. No API keys needed for this one. **1. The agent (Python).** Requires Python 3.9+. ```bash pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn ``` ```python # server.py import uuid from fastapi import FastAPI, Request from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse from ag_ui.co
